title: Organic vs. Natural: Which Label Actually Means Something?
summary: Explainer contrasting the regulated USDA Organic seal with the largely unregulated natural label.

assertions.quote: is a marketing term with no consistent meaning

verdicts.note: FDA has never formally defined 'natural' and has only an informal policy (nothing artificial or synthetic added) that does not address pesticides, processing or health; FSIS's meat definition (no artificial ingredients, minimally processed) likewise says nothing about how the animal was raised.
ERS footnote: unlike organic, natural has no legal definition in the US, and consumers and manufacturers may define it differently.

assertions.quote: Products labeled USDA organic must contain at least 95% organic ingredients
Farms undergo annual inspections, maintain detailed records, and face audits to verify compliance.
organic feed, and no antibiotics or growth hormones
Farms and producers must comply with rules prohibiting synthetic pesticides, herbicides, and genetically modified organisms
organic standards mandate access to outdoor spaces
their transparency and standards often justify the cost for those prioritizing health and sustainability
